title: Weatherproof Ventilated Transformer Cover
description: A folded-sheet cover with a steep cone roof, hooded ribbon louvers and flared side shields. It keeps rain off a pole-mounted transformer while hot air still escapes, with no custom molding.
safety: Coordinate with the utility; only qualified staff work near live equipment
Wear gloves, eye protection and a hard hat
Use fall protection when working at height
Do not work in rain, wind or lightning
mistakes: Blocking the top or bottom airflow
alternatives: Corrugated plastic or polycarbonate instead of PVC
Fiberglass panels for the side shields
tips: Use a paper pattern for the cone
Paint cut edges to prevent rust

materials.name: Angled metal strips
materials.purpose: Hooded louvers: block sideways rain, let hot air out

materials.name: Corrugated plastic or thin PVC
materials.purpose: Side shields that throw water away from base and cables

steps.title: Get approval and plan clearances
steps.text: Confirm the project with the utility that owns the transformer. Measure the unit and the pole, then set the cover size (typically 2.0–2.8 m tall, 0.5–0.8 m per side panel).
steps.safety: Never work near energized equipment. Only qualified utility personnel may de-energize, install or approach a live transformer.
steps.tip: Make a cardboard mock-up first to check clearances.

steps.title: Build the support frame
steps.text: Bolt the angle-iron frame together and keep the bottom open so cooling air can enter and crews can reach the unit.
steps.safety: Wear gloves and eye protection; cut edges are sharp.
steps.tip: Leave the base raised above ground splash.

steps.title: Fold the cone roof
steps.text: Cut the sheet to a paper pattern, fold it into a steep cone and fasten the seam. The steep angle lets water run straight down.
steps.tip: Seal rivet holes to stop leaks.

steps.title: Form the hooded louvers
steps.text: Fix angled strips in a ring under the cone so slats point downward. Air escapes sideways while rain is blocked.
steps.safety: File or fold all cut edges to avoid cuts.
steps.tip: Keep gaps even for steady airflow.

steps.title: Attach the flared side shields
steps.text: Curve thin, rigid sheets outward from the frame so surface tension carries water away from the transformer, cables and base.
steps.tip: Overlap panels a little to stop splash-through.

steps.title: Check airflow and clearances
steps.text: Confirm vents are open, nothing touches live parts, and crews can still reach the unit. Recheck bolts after the first storms.
steps.safety: This reduces rain-related risk but cannot stop failures from electrical faults, lightning or internal defects.
steps.tip: Inspect cracks, insulators and cable glands each season.

title: Floating Wall Shelf
description: Thick black floating shelves with hidden fixings, for books, lamps and photos.
safety: Use a dust mask when sanding
tips: Use a wall cleat for a clean look

steps.title: Mark the wall
steps.text: Find studs and mark a level line for the hidden cleat.
steps.safety: Check for wires and pipes before drilling.
steps.tip: Preview with painter's tape.

steps.title: Build and sand the shelf box
steps.text: Make a hollow box from a frame and two skins, leaving a slot at the back for the cleat; sand the edges smooth.
steps.safety: Wear a dust mask when sanding.

steps.title: Finish in black
steps.text: Apply thin coats of black paint, stain or oil and let each coat cure fully.
steps.safety: Lay oily rags flat to dry; they can self-ignite.

steps.title: Mount on the hidden cleat
steps.text: Screw the cleat into studs, slide the shelf over it and check it is level.
steps.tip: Test-fit before finishing.

pros: Best balance of cost and quality

title: Raised Garden Planter
description: A row of five connected planter boxes with brown woven-look panels and black corner posts, sized for peppers, tomatoes, carrots and potatoes.
safety: Wear a dust mask with dry potting mix
tips: Water at soil level in the morning

steps.title: Choose and level the site
steps.text: Pick a spot with 6+ hours of sun and level the ground.
steps.tip: Mark the row with stakes.

steps.title: Join panels and corner posts
steps.text: Press the panels into the corner posts to form a square box; tap them home with a rubber mallet.
steps.tip: Line up the panel ribs before pressing.

steps.title: Connect the boxes in a row
steps.text: Clip the boxes together side by side and check the row is straight.

steps.title: Line, fill and plant
steps.text: Add drainage mesh, fill with soil and plant peppers, tomatoes, carrots and potatoes.
steps.safety: Wear gloves and lift soil with your knees.
steps.tip: Group plants with similar needs in one box.

title: Garage Workbench
description: A rolling 1.5 m workbench with a steel frame, locking casters and a hardwood butcher-block top, with a pegboard wall above for tools.
safety: Wear eye and ear protection and gloves
Lock the casters whenever you work
Use welding PPE if you weld
tips: Oil the top before first use
Fit adjustable feet if the floor slopes

steps.title: Cut the steel tube
steps.text: Cut legs, rails and stretchers to length from square steel tube; deburr every cut end.
steps.safety: Wear eye and ear protection and gloves when cutting steel.
steps.tip: Cut identical parts together for matching lengths.

steps.title: Assemble the steel frame
steps.text: Bolt (or weld) the legs and rails into two end frames, then join them with long stretchers. Check for square.
steps.safety: If welding, use a welding helmet and keep flammables clear.
steps.tip: Diagonal measurements match when square.

steps.title: Fit the casters
steps.text: Bolt a caster to the foot of each leg and check the frame sits level.
steps.safety: Lock all casters before loading the bench.
steps.tip: Locking swivel casters suit a rolling bench.

steps.title: Make and fit the butcher-block top
steps.text: Glue and clamp hardwood strips into a solid top, sand smooth, oil it and fix it to the frame with brackets.
steps.tip: Add a pegboard above the bench for hanging tools.
